findings.explanation: The route omits all of next_hop_gateway/next_hop_ilb/next_hop_instance/next_hop_ip/next_hop_vpn_tunnel, one of which is required by the provider schema. `terraform validate` currently fails on this resource, which means validate.sh/validate.ps1 (both run `terraform validate` against this example) and any CI gate that calls them are broken on the current tree.
findings.remediation: Set next_hop_gateway to the default internet gateway.
findings.title: Example fails terraform validate: route has no next-hop target

findings.explanation: `key_ring = google_kms_key_ring.static` passes the whole resource object where a string self-link/id is required. `terraform validate` fails with "Inappropriate value for attribute \"key_ring\": string required, but have object". This is a second independent blocker (alongside HOLDEN_BP_001) preventing the example — and therefore validate.sh/validate.ps1 — from validating at all.
findings.remediation: Reference the key ring's id attribute instead of the resource object.
findings.title: Example fails terraform validate: key_ring passed a resource object instead of its id

findings.explanation: location = "west-europe" is Azure's region naming convention. GCP KMS locations use names like "europe-west1" or "global". Even after fixing HOLDEN_BP_002, `terraform apply` will fail with a 400 from the KMS API because this location does not exist in GCP.
findings.remediation: Use a real GCP KMS location, e.g. europe-west1.
findings.title: KMS key ring location is an Azure region name, not a valid GCP location

findings.explanation: main.tf contains only a comment; there is no `terraform { required_providers { ... } }` block anywhere in the root module. Only the example (example/examplea/terraform.tf) pins a google provider version. Consumers of this module have no compatibility guardrail and can plan against an incompatible google provider version. Because the block is entirely absent (not just missing an attribute), holden's existing HLD_TF_001/002/054 checks don't fire — there's no `terraform` resource instance for them to evaluate.
findings.remediation: Add a versions.tf declaring required_providers (google, with a version range, not an exact pin since this is a reusable module) and required_version.
findings.title: Root module declares no required_providers/required_version

findings.explanation: The description reads "not optional ... Leave null if not using CSEK", but the variable has no default and its validation block requires length(var.kms_key_self_link) > 0 — so it can never actually be left null/empty. A module consumer following the description will pass null and hit the validation error instead of the documented behavior.
findings.fix: description = "KMS key self link used to encrypt the boot disk (CSEK). Required."
findings.remediation: Rewrite the description to match the actual (required, non-empty) contract, e.g. "KMS key self link used to encrypt the boot disk (CSEK). Required."
findings.title: kms_key_self_link description contradicts its own validation

findings.explanation: f1-micro is an older shared-core machine type. e2-micro offers better price/performance and, in eligible regions (including this module's default zone us-central1-a), qualifies for the GCP Always Free tier the same way f1-micro historically did.
findings.title: machine_type default is the legacy f1-micro shared-core type
